threats.title: Forged deployment events create misleading notifications
threats.description: An Internet-based attacker forges deployment events by sending arbitrary JSON payloads to the public Event Receiver endpoint. The receiver accepts and processes any well-formed delivery without verifying CI signatures, so it cannot distinguish forged requests from legitimate ones sent by the CI platform. The forged events are passed to the Chat Notifier, which posts deployment notifications into the internal chat channel. Engineers relying on the channel see notifications for deployments that did not occur, or with incorrect repository, environment, or commit information.
preconditions: The Event Receiver (cmp-001) exposes a public, internet-accessible HTTPS endpoint for receiving deployment events from the CI platform over df-001.
The Event Receiver accepts and processes any well-formed JSON delivery and does not verify CI signatures on incoming events, so it cannot authenticate the true sender of a request.
An attacker is able to send HTTP requests with arbitrary JSON bodies to the Event Receiver’s public URL.
attack_path: Attacker discovers or guesses the Event Receiver’s public HTTPS URL that the CI platform uses for deployment webhooks.
Attacker crafts an HTTP POST request with a JSON body containing chosen repository_name, environment, and commit_identifier fields (or other fields the receiver uses).
The Event Receiver (cmp-001) receives the request over HTTPS (df-001) and, because it accepts any well-formed delivery without checking a signature, parses the JSON as a valid deployment event.
The Event Receiver forwards the parsed event to the Chat Notifier (cmp-002) over its internal channel (df-002).
The Chat Notifier formats the event into a deployment notification message and calls the chat platform’s API (cmp-004) over df-003, posting into the internal chat channel.
Engineers reading the chat channel see the forged notification and may believe a deployment occurred, or occurred in a particular repository/environment/commit, when it did not.
threats.impact: Integrity of deployment events (ast-001) and deployment notifications in the chat channel (ast-002) is compromised: attackers can inject arbitrary or misleading deployment records into the operational view engineers rely on. This can cause engineers to misinterpret what has been deployed where, potentially leading to mistaken operational actions or eroding trust in the chat channel as a source of truth, even though the events themselves only contain repository names, environments, and commit identifiers rather than customer data.

threats.title: Flood or malformed deployment events degrade Deploy Notifier availability
threats.description: An attacker sends a high volume of deployment-event requests, or very large/malformed JSON payloads, to the public Event Receiver endpoint. Because the receiver parses each JSON body and hands events to the Chat Notifier, processing these requests consumes CPU, memory, and outbound API capacity. Under sufficient load, the Event Receiver or Chat Notifier may slow down, fail, or be unable to process legitimate deployment events from the CI platform in a timely manner, reducing or temporarily blocking engineers’ visibility into real deployments.
preconditions: The Event Receiver (cmp-001) exposes a public, internet-accessible HTTPS endpoint that accepts deployment events from the CI platform over df-001.
The Event Receiver parses incoming JSON deployment events and hands them to the Chat Notifier (cmp-002) for further processing (df-002).
An attacker is able to send deployment-event HTTP requests to the Event Receiver at a rate or size that approaches or exceeds what the service and its environment can comfortably process.
attack_path: Attacker identifies the public HTTPS URL used by the CI platform to deliver deployment events to the Event Receiver.
Attacker scripts a client to send a large number of deployment-event POST requests, or unusually large/malformed JSON bodies, to the Event Receiver over df-001.
The Event Receiver parses each incoming JSON body and attempts to act on the event, consuming CPU, memory, and network resources.
For events that parse successfully, the Event Receiver forwards them to the Chat Notifier over df-002, which further consumes resources formatting and posting messages.

Under sustained load, the Event Receiver or Chat Notifier becomes slow, resource constrained, or unstable, causing legitimate deployment events from the CI platform to be delayed, dropped, or never posted to the chat platform.
Engineers relying on chat notifications lose timely visibility into actual deployments because genuine events are not processed or delivered reliably.
threats.impact: Availability and reliability of deployment events (ast-001) and deployment notifications in the chat channel (ast-002) are reduced: during or after a flood, legitimate deployment events may be delayed, dropped, or not posted, leaving engineers without an accurate, timely view of what has been deployed. This can hinder incident response and coordination around real deploys, even though the underlying data does not contain customer information.
